RUS 1105.title: Elementary Russian
RUS 1105.description: Fundamentals of grammar, pronunciation, conversation, and reading. Respond to simple questions using appropriate grammar and syntax, participate in conversation about family, school, everyday situations, etc., write in cursive, and read adapted texts. 1105: Grammar and conversation; 1106: Grammar, conversation, and reading.

RUS 1106.title: Elementary Russian
RUS 1106.description: Fundamentals of grammar, pronunciation, conversation, and reading. Respond to simple questions using appropriate grammar and syntax, participate in conversation about family, school, everyday situations, etc., write in cursive, and read adapted texts. 1105: Grammar and conversation; 1106: Grammar, conversation, and reading.

RUS 1114.title: Accelerated Elementary Russian
RUS 1114.description: Proficiency-oriented approach to elementary Russian, designed for learners who wish to progress rapidly through the beginning stages of language learning. Develops the four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing) in a cultural context. Duplicates 1105 and 1106.

RUS 2105.title: Intermediate Russian
RUS 2105.description: Grammar, reading, conversation, and composition. Emphasizes comprehension of written and spoken Russian.

RUS 2106.title: Intermediate Russian
RUS 2106.description: Grammar, reading, conversation, and composition. Emphasizes comprehension of written and spoken Russian.

RUS 2114.title: Accelerated Intermediate Russian
RUS 2114.description: Proficiency-oriented approach to intermediate Russian for learners who wish to progress rapidly through the intermediate stages of language learning. Develops the four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing) in a cultural context. Duplicates 2105 and 2106.

RUS 2724.title: Magic, Ritual, and Mythology
RUS 2724.description: Analysis of folklore, society, and culture in Slavic written and visual texts and speech communities, including the Russian-speaking world. Evaluation of multiple sources to interrogate dominant stereotypes associated with the Russian-speaking world. Application of foundational theories and approaches to the study of Slavic folklore in historical, social, political, and geographic contexts. Fostering of cross-cultural awareness and intercultural understanding by comparing Slavic folkways with those of the West, the US, and Appalachia. Taught in English.

RUS 2734.title: Introduction to Russian Culture and Civilization
RUS 2734.description: Introduction to Russian Culture and Civilization. Interactions between major political and historical events, social and artistic movements in Russia. Russian literature, art, architecture, film, and theatre in the context of Russian cultural history. Aesthetic and rhetorical strategies. Interpretation of intercultural experiences from different vantage points. Taught in English.

RUS 3105.title: Grammar, Composition and Conversation
RUS 3105.description: Detailed study of grammar. Practice in written and oral expression in Russian on a variety of topics. Supplementary readings to emphasize application of grammatical principles. 3105 includes a rapid grammatical review.

RUS 3106.title: Grammar, Composition and Conversation
RUS 3106.description: Detailed study of grammar. Practice in written and oral expression in Russian on a variety of topics. Supplementary readings to emphasize application of grammatical principles. 3105 includes a rapid grammatical review.

RUS 3114.title: Accelerated Advanced Russian Grammar Conversation Composition
RUS 3114.description: Proficiency-oriented approach to advanced Russian. Daily progression through advanced Russian grammar, conversation and composition. Accelerated development of the four language modalities (speaking, listening, reading, writing) in a cultural context. Short translations and paraphrases of authentic Russian texts. Duplicates RUS 3105 and 3106.

RUS 3124.title: Russian for Oral Proficiency
RUS 3124.description: Acquisition of spoken/conversational Russian and enhancement of listening comprehension in a wide variety of common conversational situations. Listening in Russian at an intermediate to advanced level to comprehend native speech. Conversation in Russian at intermediate to advanced levels to create paragraph-length discourse and respond to demands and/or complications in spoken Russian appropriate to professional and academic contexts, as well as personal and home environments.

RUS 3304.title: Survey of Nineteenth-Century Russian Literature in Translation
RUS 3304.description: Masterpieces of Russian fiction and poetry written between 1815 and 1881. Romantic poetry of the early nineteenth century and traces the beginnings of Russian prose from early short stories to the rise of the novel as the dominant literary form in the second half of the century. History and politics to theological and philosophical issues in various works. Methods, terminology and practice of literary analysis. Taught in English.

RUS 3314.title: Survey of Twentieth-Century Russian Literature in Translation
RUS 3314.description: Masterpieces of the twentieth-century Russian literature. Symbolist, Acmeist and Futurist poetry, modernist and postmodernist prose such as Mikhail Bulgakovs The Master and Margarita, and Viktor Pelevins Life of Insects. Terminology, practice, and standard methods of literary analysis. Interactions between major political events, social and literary movement. Aesthetic and rhetorical strategies. Taught in English.

RUS 3424.title: Topics in Russian Literature in English
RUS 3424.description: Variable-content course devoted to the study of Russian literary classics. From general surveys of nineteenth- and twentieth-century literature to more intensive study of the works of a single major author. Aesthetic and rhetorical strategies. Interactions between literary movements and political, historical, and cultural events. May be repeated once with different content for a maximum of 6 credits. Readings and lectures in English. No knowledge of Russian required.

RUS 3434.title: The Works of Vladimir Nabokov
RUS 3434.description: Readings in major works of Vladimir Nabokov from the 1920s through the 1970s. Aesthetic and rhetorical strategies, literary analysis, major themes, immigration and cultural knowledge. Taught in English.

RUS 3474.title: Russian and Soviet Cinema
RUS 3474.description: Exploration of Russian and Soviet cinema from the 1890s to the present day. Evaluation of film techniques and narrative approaches. Discussion of Socialist Realism, propaganda and agitka (short informational films) as well as auteur cinema and filmmakers. Comparison of the various historical, political and artistic movements in cinema from Imperial Russia through the fall of the Soviet Union. Taught in English.

RUS 3534.title: Russian as a Global Language
RUS 3534.description: Exploration of Russian as a global language across Russian-speaking countries. Examination of the role of Russian in business, diplomacy, and cultural exchange in various countries in regions such as Central Asia, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus, and the Baltic region. Development of professional and region-specific vocabulary. Comparison and contrast of cross-cultural communication among local cultures in professional interactions. Application of Russian to international career contexts. Analysis of authentic materials produced in Russian. Taught in Russian.

RUS 4104.title: Professional Communication in Russia
RUS 4104.description: Task-based approach to professional communication in Russian. Progression through topics of advanced Russian grammar, conversation, interpretation, and composition of professional documents. Practice and application of professional communication skills (inform, instruct, persuade, request, and respond) and vocabulary in a variety of Russian-speaking professional contexts. Examination of professional practices and customs in professional settings with authentic materials.

RUS 4114.title: Sounds of Russian
RUS 4114.description: Analysis of the Russian sound system, including the relationship between speech and the written language. Description of Russian vowels and consonants, employing applicable terminology of phonetics and phonology. Examination of intonation constructions and stress patterns. Comparison and contrast of the sound systems of Russian and English. Interpretation of social meaning of regional variation of Russian through a broad range of authentic materials. Taught in Russian.

RUS 4204.title: Topics in Russian Culture and Civilization
RUS 4204.description: Specific topics in Russian culture and civilization. Variable content. May be repeated for credit with different content.

RUS 4304.title: Studies in Russian Literature
RUS 4304.description: Selected masterpieces of Russian literature, read in original. Lectures and discussions in Russian. May be repeated for credit with different content.
